resources.string: Android plays a short animation for every window, transition and UI change. The three animation scales (Developer options) multiply their duration. 0.5× halves the time you wait for each transition. It makes the phone feel faster; it does not make the processor faster.

Apps can run jobs, alarms and services in the background even when you never open them. Setting the RUN_ANY_IN_BACKGROUND app-op to \"ignore\" is the same switch as Android\'s \"Restricted\" battery setting: the app can no longer run in the background, but works normally when you open it. Only apps you haven\'t opened for 30 days are suggested.
Shizuku or root, plus usage access

Apps on the battery-optimization exemption list (\"Unrestricted\") ignore Doze and App Standby, so they can wake the phone at any time. Removing an exemption you don\'t need lets Android batch their work while the phone is idle. Messaging, alarm and fitness apps may need the exemption: keep those.
Shizuku or root (or change each app in Settings)

Location, microphone, camera, contacts, SMS and call log access are the permissions with the biggest privacy impact, and background location also costs battery. Revoking a permission is instant and reversible: the app asks again when it needs it.

Since Android 13 posting notifications is a runtime permission (POST_NOTIFICATIONS). Revoking it for apps that only send promotions silences them completely. Every notification also wakes the screen and the app, so fewer notifications means fewer wake-ups.
Android 13+. Shizuku or root (or change each app in Settings)

Apps keep cache files to load faster. The cache is rebuilt when needed, so clearing it is safe, but the apps will be a bit slower the first time and re-download thumbnails. Prune asks Android to trim caches the same way it does when storage runs low (pm trim-caches) and measures the space actually freed.
Usage access to see sizes; Shizuku or root to clear all caches at once

Shows which apps you use most (screen time, last 7 days) and the battery estimate Android itself calculates (dumpsys batterystats, since the last full charge). Use it to find apps that cost more than they are worth.
Usage access; battery estimates need Shizuku or root

After app updates Android runs apps partly interpreted until its idle maintenance compiles them during the night (while charging). Running the same background compilation job now (cmd package bg-dexopt-job) compiles the hot code paths of every app with its usage profile. Takes several minutes and uses battery.
Off removes animations completely. Some apps rely on animations to show progress; 0.5× is the usual choice.
Clear cached files of all apps
Setting them to 0.5× halves transition time. %1$s
Lets Prune find apps you don\'t use and show storage per app.
Restrict their background activity or uninstall them.
Review which of them really need to run unrestricted.
